classification_basis: reference factory rectangle fitted to one horizontal platform plane using known ground-support provenance; qualify by footprint/perimeter clearance while reporting cliff-only vertical-layer ambiguity

small.intent: local or satellite production; limited expansion

medium.intent: dedicated factory with meaningful miner/belt upgrade headroom

large.intent: major production district intended to survive multiple throughput upgrades

very_large.intent: regional or late-game industrial campus where terrain should not be the primary growth constraint

workable.interpretation: placement zone with some directional constraint

poor.interpretation: highly elongated placement zone; rectangle location is more informative than region shape

notes: Every qualifying rectangle is one flat horizontal platform. Its Z is fitted to the highest known ground-support cell in the footprint.

Landscape (provenance 1) and fill (3) are treated as ground support. Cliff surfaces (4/5) are not assumed to be ground because the 2.5D heightfield may be showing an overhead rock or natural bridge instead of the usable floor beneath.

A footprint may contain a limited fraction of cliff-only/unknown ground cells. Defaults require at least 85% known ground across the footprint and 75% around the perimeter; ambiguity is emitted as a metric rather than silently interpreted.
At 16 m working resolution each support cell uses the median of its underlying known-ground samples. Decrease working resolution to make smaller terrain details matter.

For a tolerance T, the lowest no-penetration platform is fitted at the highest known ground cell and known-ground maximum clearance must also be <= T. At T=4 m this approximates a 4 m foundation remaining terrain-supported rather than visibly floating.

The PHM_steel_deck_502094 calibration fixture is a 221-foundation flat 4 m deck. On known landscape/fill centers its top is ~3.0 m above terrain median, 3.8 m at p95; 42 centers coincide with cliff/overhead top-surface provenance and are kept separate from support clearance.
The irregular region is only the connected zone of qualifying rectangle centers. Emitted rectangles and fitted platform elevations are the primary planning geometry.
build_surfaces_v5 remains available as the all-top-surface plane-fit baseline; v4 and v3 remain alternate analyses.
